signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + CPI Repricing
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records USD up +0.877% across 9 pairs against NOK down −1.932% across 2 pairs, establishing a 2.809% leader-to-laggard divergence. Spot trades at 9.506 after a wide-range expansion bar cleared the prior 10-day closing high, lifting price above its SMA20 at 9.354, SMA50 at 9.406, and SMA200 at 9.488. The move is reinforced by hotter October US CPI and hawkish rhetoric from Fed Governor Bowman, which drove US 10Y yields toward 4.983%. Real policy differentials remain narrow with the Fed at +1.61% against Norges Bank at +1.82%, but short-term momentum favors continued greenback dominance. However, retail positioning shows an extreme 91% long concentration, raising exhaustion risk if follow-through falters. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, momentum-led continuation supported by G10 divergence. Catalyst: Norges Bank Financial Stability Report 11 Nov. Risk: Spot closes back below the SMA200 at 9.488, triggering an unwind of extended retail longs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Downside Hedging
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.71, holding above its SMA20 at 157.95, SMA50 at 157.24, and SMA200 at 158.61 after clearing local resistance at 158.47. A 265bp OIS carry premium via SOFR 3.88% versus TONA 1.23% sustains the structural bid on the pair. However, the Saxo 25-delta 1M risk reversal registers an acute put skew of −1.99, showing that options participants are heavily hedging spot downside despite the spot rally. COT leveraged funds hold a modest net short of −21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile of their 52-week range, indicating that speculative carry exposure is stretched. With spot testing 158.80, 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention commentary. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; structural carry support offset by aggressive downside options skew. Catalyst: Fed Vice Chair Barr speech 11 Nov. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 prompts official intervention rhetoric, accelerating put-driven downside.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + BEER Undervaluation
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1172, remaining trapped below its SMA20 at 1.1197, SMA50 at 1.1330, and SMA200 at 1.1542. Leveraged funds are net short −104,030 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of their 52-week range with a z-score of −1.80, reflecting deeply crowded institutional short positioning. The BEER equilibrium framework calculates spot at a z-score of −3.20σ cheap versus its 1.1319 fair value, highlighting stretched structural undervaluation. Nominal policy spreads favor the dollar with the Fed at 4.00% against the ECB at 2.65% for a 135bp spread, though 1M ATM implied volatility sits low at 5.8% against HV30 of 4.7%. A lack of downside follow-through below 1.1166 leaves the crowded short base vulnerable to short-covering on any hawkish European data surprise. Trade bias: Long EUR/USD, contrarian mean-reversion against a crowded institutional short. Catalyst: Germany CPI release 11 Nov — 2.8% YoY forecast. Risk: Daily close below 1.1150 invalidates the base and extends the technical downtrend.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Breakdown + Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6871, extending a firm technical downtrend below its falling SMA20 at 0.6984, SMA50 at 0.7037, and SMA200 at 0.7059. Spot closed below key support at 0.6905, leaving the pair stretched 2.43 ATR below its 20-day moving average following hot US CPI releases. The price breakdown directly contradicts underlying carry dynamics, where RBA AONIA at 4.85% offers a 97bp premium over Fed SOFR at 3.88%. Leveraged funds maintain a net long position of +43,532 contracts, but persistent liquidation over the past four weeks indicates speculative capitulation. With 1M options displaying a −1.10 risk reversal put skew and retail sentiment heavily biased at 70% long, downside momentum retains technical control. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, trend continuation following support violation. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims 11 Nov. Risk: Daily recovery back above 0.6905 re-engages the 97bp AUD carry advantage and forces short covering.
